title: Comparing the Effectiveness of Propensity Score-Matched Ab Interno Trabeculotomy Between Two Types of Trabecular Hooks

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 unported, incorporated in Dove Medical Press terms (article <license>); non-commercial, therefore private

indication: glaucoma with concurrent cataract, progression not controlled by medication alone, no previous glaucoma surgery: POAG, NTG, PXG, secondary open-angle and chronic angle-closure glaucoma; KDB and TMH eyes propensity-score matched 1:1 on preoperative medication score and disease type; minimum follow-up 6 months; retrospective single-center (Japan)

groups.description: ab interno trabeculotomy with the Kahook Dual Blade (about 3-6 clock hours) after phacoemulsification; 24 eyes of 19 patients (t0001!R2C2)
ab interno trabeculotomy with the Tanito microhook (about 3-8 clock hours) after phacoemulsification; 24 eyes of 17 patients (t0001!R2C3)

series.baseline_label: Table 2 row 'Baseline' (Methods: baseline IOP = final IOP measured preoperatively; same cell text as Table 1 'IOP (mmHg), mean ± SD', t0001!R7C2)
series.notes: column 'IOP at each time point (mmHg), mean ± SD' under 'KDB Group (n=24)'; rows 1 month, 3 months (± 2 weeks), 6 months (± 4 weeks); per-visit n not tabulated; Table 6 reports additional glaucoma filtration surgery in 1 KDB eye, and the article does not state whether that eye's IOP was censored or kept in the Table 2 means

series.baseline_label: Table 2 row 'Baseline' (same cell text as Table 1 'IOP (mmHg), mean ± SD', t0001!R7C3)
series.notes: column 'IOP at each time point (mmHg), mean ± SD' under 'TMH Group (n=24)'; rows 1 month, 3 months (± 2 weeks), 6 months (± 4 weeks); per-visit n not tabulated; Table 6 reports additional glaucoma filtration surgery in 4 TMH eyes, and the article does not state whether their IOP was censored or kept in the Table 2 means

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': surgery was indicated for progression not controlled with medication alone, preoperative medication scores are tabulated (t0001!R6C2, t0001!R6C3), the baseline IOP is the last preoperative IOP, IOP-lowering medications were re-administered postoperatively on the surgeon's recommendation; no washout described.
Tonometer not stated in the article, so method 'unstated'.

Both arms are standard ab interno trabeculotomy instruments chosen at the surgeon's discretion, compared without an investigational agent, so both are 'control' groups; both eyes of some patients are included (24 eyes of 19 and of 17 patients).
Selection: propensity matching on preoperative covariates (medication score, disease type) and a minimum 6-month follow-up; no postoperative-outcome selection of the Table 2 analysis set is stated.
Medication scores (combination drops = 2, oral acetazolamide = 1) are tabulated in Table 3 (not extracted).
